reed_thatch.why: Thatch bundles give way to slate and tile once Craft Row can cut them.

wooden_bowl.why: Pottery bowls arrive with Market Day; carved wood fades out.

mud_clogs.why: The last pair of clogs sells before boots reach the shelf at Market Day.

wading_staff.why: Once the Chapel stands the Ford is crossed on a laid plank, not a wading staff.

straw.why: The stable lane takes over bedding straw by the bale.

oat_cake.why: The oat cake is a crossing's bread; a village bakes rye.

barley_broth.why: A bowl of broth gives way to the Market Day pie.

bramble_jam.why: Hedge jam is what a crossing has; fruit preserves outsell it.

reed_basket.why: The market basket replaces the reed one the week the first stall opens.

tinderbox.why: Craft Row sells a lantern that keeps its flame; the tinderbox is a crossing's tool.

clay_pot.why: Glazed pots from the potter's row outlast the crossing's clay.

hurdle.why: Hurdles are for sheep. The pens go to stone and rail.

wattle_panel.why: Wattle fences give way to timber and Craft Row joinery.

oak_pail.why: Coopers' hooped pails replace the plain oak bucket.

goose.why: Live geese leave the shelf once Market Day has a pie stall.

butter_churn.why: The hamlet churn is a household job; by Market Day butter comes in tubs.

sack_beans.why: Dry beans fade as the market stocks barley and bacon.

pot_barley.why: A barley pot is a hamlet's supper; the Garrison feeds on flour and hardtack.

smoked_eel.why: The ford's eel is dear to a hamlet; a chapel town eats ham.

laying_hen.why: Hens move to the town's own coops; the shelf stops selling them at Craft Row.

travel_satchel.why: The chapman's pack outsells the satchel once the road is busy.

scarecrow.why: The fields are walled in at the Garrison; there is no call for a scarecrow.

pattens.why: Pattens lift a shoe out of the mud; the streets are laid by Craft Row.

stall_canvas.why: Stall canvas gives way to the guild's own pavilion cloth.

toy_horse.why: The wooden horse is a Market Day toy; the Garrison children play at drill.

juggling_balls.why: The jugglers move on; the dice-men stay.

chapmans_pack.why: A pedlar's pack has no place on the shelf once the town has shops of its own.

tally_sticks.why: Tally sticks are for illiterate counters; the guild teaches the counting frame.

torches.why: Pitch torches go out when the street lamps are lit.

cider_jug.why: Cider is a village drink; Market Town prefers mead and wine.

sheepskin.why: Sheepskin is a hamlet's coat; a garrison town buys wool and sentry cloaks.

bunting.why: Bunting belongs to Market Day; walled towns hang banners instead.

bale_tags.why: Hand-tied tags give way to the guild's stamped waybill.

hand_bell.why: The hand bell is a crier's tool; a walled town has a crier and a bell-tower.

seedcorn.why: The town grows its own seed by Craft Row; the caravans stop carrying it.

plough_irons.why: The smiths forge ploughshares locally once Craft Row smokes.

sickles.why: Sickles are forged in town from Market Day.

oatmeal.why: A chapel town mills its own oats.

rough_cloth.why: Rough cloth is a hamlet's lack; Market Day buys linen.

bee_skeps.why: The town keeps its own bees from the Village on.

flax_sheaves.why: Flax is grown near; the loom frames take over.

hurdle_bundles.why: Hurdles are made in the pens at the Village.

barley_seed.why: Seed is saved from the town's own fields once the Garrison stands.

ox_yokes.why: Yokes are carved in town; wheels still come in.

tar_barrels.why: Pitch is boiled in town from Craft Row on.

hemp_bundles.why: Hemp goes in by the bundle till the ropewalk opens.

live_poultry.why: Market Town has its own poultry yard.

caged_songbirds.why: The songbird fashion fades once the Garrison drills.

wool_fleeces.why: Raw fleeces give way to dyed wool.

hide_bales.why: Tanneries open at Craft Row; raw hides stop coming.

rawhides.why: Raw hides stop at Craft Row.

salt_fish.why: Salt fish gives way to barrelled herring.

cider_casks.why: Cider casks stop when mead and wine come in.

trade_stock._note: C-53 (C4.2). Which SHOP sells what. Five trades. Every shop_stock key is carried by exactly one trade (listed in that trade's 'carries'); a trade also sells its own_goods (new goods that exist ONLY here, keyed {name,cost,flavour,tier} plus optional last_tier). A trade's shelf at growth tier N = the keys in 'carries' and 'own_goods' where max(good.tier, trade.opens_tier) <= N and (no stock_retirement.shop_goods last_tier, or N <= last_tier). own_goods carry their own last_tier where they leave. 'schedule' lists, per tier, what ENTERS and what LEAVES that trade's shelf at that tier (precomputed from the rule above; they agree). A trade does not exist before opens_tier: no smithy before tier 3, no apothecary before 4, no stables before 5. Dead until wired.

bad_rope.name: Knotted Rope

reed_mat.name: Reed Mat

oiled_rain_cape.name: Oiled Rain Cape
oiled_rain_cape.flavour: Keeps off the Bellmire drizzle for one wet winter.

street_pie.name: Hot Street Pie

stoppered_bottle.name: Stoppered Glass Bottle

guild.name: Guild Counter

contract_form.name: Contract Form
contract_form.flavour: Blank, ruled, ready to be regretted.

toll_tokens.name: String of Toll Tokens
toll_tokens.flavour: Pay the Ford. Keep the string.

bonded_satchel.name: Bonded Satchel

escort_writ.name: Writ of Escort
escort_writ.flavour: Names the guards a caravan is owed.

guild_ring.name: Guild Signet Ring
guild_ring.flavour: Sealing wax and standing, in one.

smith.name: Smithy

bog_iron_knife.name: Bog-Iron Knife

ploughshare.flavour: Bites the bank-soil. Heavier than it looks.

kettle_hook.name: Kettle Hook
kettle_hook.flavour: Iron S for a pot over a fire.

mail_hauberk.name: Mail Hauberk
mail_hauberk.flavour: Heavy. Counts the cost of every blow it stops.

plate_gauntlets.name: Plate Gauntlets
plate_gauntlets.flavour: The first plate a Bellmire smith will sign.

plate_cuirass.name: Plate Cuirass
plate_cuirass.flavour: A city's armour. More than a crossing's mail, and worth it.

apothecary.voice: Tell me where it hurts and what you can pay.

poppy_milk.flavour: Sold by the thimble to people who can pay by the thimble.

rosewater.name: Rosewater Flask
rosewater.flavour: The apothecary's one concession to beauty.

theriac.flavour: Sixty ingredients and a cure for most things.

stables.voice: Hay, harness, and horses with opinions.

horseshoe_set.flavour: Four shoes, forty nails, one patient horse.

halter.flavour: Leads a cow, a pony, or a drunk.

bridle.name: Leather Bridle

caravan_manifests._note: C-53 (C4.3). What a caravan ARRIVES carrying. A tier-1 crossing has no caravans. At growth tier N the town can receive any caravan with first_tier <= N (cumulative; a caravan never stops coming). One arrival delivers: (a) its 'cargo' lines - qty of each trader_cargo good, worth cargo_value gold in all, which is what bandits are after - and (b) its 'supply' lines - the units of each supply resource the town RECEIVES when the caravan arrives. units = qty of the source cargo x supply_resources[resource].units_per_qty, summed over the cargo lines that feed that resource; gold_value = units x supply_resources[resource].unit_cost; supply_gold_value is the sum. If the caravan is TAKEN instead of arriving, the town receives none of its supply units (cargo lines are lost with it): the whole supply list is the cost of losing it. A unit is one shelf unit of the goods named in supply_resources[resource].restocks (e.g. 6 units of grain = 6 shelf units across Sack of Grain and Loaf). guards = armed men riding with it. Cargo lines with no 'from' source in supply_resources (spice, silk, glassware...) are trade goods only: they enrich the town but restock no shelf. Dead until wired.

price_ladders._note: C-53 (C4.4). Price sanity, checked by script. Each ladder is a class of goods listed in order of tier; cost and tier are both non-decreasing down the list, so a later (grander) good is never cheaper than an earlier one - a city's plate is never cheaper than a crossing's mail, a lord's saddle never cheaper than a halter. Keys may be shop_stock, trader_cargo or trade_stock own_goods. Costs are flat across tiers: the same good costs the same at tier 2 and tier 12. Dead until wired.
